skill.name: fiftyone-develop-plugin
skill.description: Develop custom FiftyOne plugins, including Python operators, Python panels, and JavaScript panels. Use this skill to plan plugin structure, generate implementation files, install locally, test in the FiftyOne App, and iterate on user feedback.
skill.summary: Build, test, and refine custom FiftyOne operators and panels.
skill.author: AdonaiVera

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent or prompt injection was found. The static findings are documentation examples for FiftyOne plugin development, including expected local plugin installation, placeholder API usage, and reference links.

remediation.issue: External API examples could be copied without a privacy review.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to confirm endpoints, data fields, and user consent before sending dataset metadata to external services.

remediation.issue: Local install examples write into the FiftyOne plugins directory.
remediation.suggestion: State that copy and symlink commands should only run after the user approves the target plugin directory.

remediation.issue: The exporter example accepts a user provided output path.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend validating output paths and asking before overwriting existing files.

| `"grid modal"` | Panel can appear in either location |

content.value_statement: FiftyOne plugin work can require many files, APIs, and testing steps. This skill guides agents through planning, code generation, local install, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirements gathering for custom FiftyOne plugins.
Plans plugin file structure and manifest fields.
Explains Python operator patterns, inputs, outputs, and placements.
Explains Python panel layout, state, data, and event handlers.
Explains JavaScript panel setup with React and build commands.
Provides local install and testing steps for the FiftyOne App.
limitations: Generated plugins still need user review before running locally.
External API integrations require user supplied endpoints and credentials.
JavaScript panels require Node.js and the FiftyOne JavaScript tooling.
The skill does not guarantee compatibility with every FiftyOne release.

use_cases.title: Create A Dataset Operator
use_cases.description: Build a Python operator that processes samples, collects user inputs, and reports progress in the FiftyOne App.

use_cases.title: Design An Analysis Panel
use_cases.description: Create a panel that displays dataset statistics, controls, charts, and stateful interactions for repeated review work.

use_cases.title: Prototype A React Panel
use_cases.description: Set up a JavaScript panel with React components, registration, build scripts, and local testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Simple Operator
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal FiftyOne operator that shows one text input and returns a success message. Ask setup questions before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Statistics Panel
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a FiftyOne panel for dataset statistics. Include the file structure, manifest fields, and a short test plan before coding.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Label Exporter
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a FiftyOne operator that exports selected labels to a user chosen file. Validate inputs and avoid overwriting files without confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Create A React Panel
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a JavaScript FiftyOne panel with React controls for searching and selecting samples. Include build steps, registration, and local testing guidance.

output_examples.input: I need a plugin that exports labels from selected samples.
output: A requirements checklist for selected samples, label fields, output path, and overwrite behavior.
A planned plugin structure with manifest, operator file, and test steps.
A generated operator workflow that exports labels and reports progress.

output_examples.input: Create a panel that shows dataset statistics.
output: A panel design with state fields, refresh behavior, and chart data requirements.
Implementation guidance for rendering counts, label distributions, and a refresh button.
A local verification checklist for opening the panel in the FiftyOne App.

output_examples.input: Help me make a JavaScript panel for browsing samples.
output: A React panel plan with search, sort, selection, and plugin registration details.
Build and install instructions for local development.
Testing steps for refreshing the app and checking sample interactions.

best_practices: Approve the plugin plan before generating files or running install commands.
Keep secrets in FiftyOne secret configuration and never hardcode credential values.
Test operators and panels on a small dataset before using production data.
anti_patterns: Do not copy plugins into the local plugins directory without user approval.
Do not call external APIs with dataset metadata before reviewing privacy impact.
Do not overwrite export files unless the user confirms the destination.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create FiftyOne Python operators, Python panels, and JavaScript panels.

faq.question: Can it create a complete plugin structure?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan and generate the manifest, Python files, JavaScript files, and dependency files.

faq.question: Does it run the plugin automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides local install and test steps that should run only after user approval.

faq.question: Can it work with external APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. External API work needs user supplied endpoints, secrets, and privacy review.

faq.question: Is JavaScript panel support included?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers React panel setup, registration, build commands, and local development flow.

faq.question: What should users review before publishing?
faq.answer: Review file writes, external requests, secrets, dependencies, and plugin install commands.
